defects.justification: The size limit is checked only after Rack has already parsed and written the whole multipart body to a tempfile, so an arbitrarily large upload still uses disk, time and bandwidth before getting a 413. Enforce the limit on Content-Length or the request stream (or at the proxy) before parsing.

Untrusted user uploads go to ImageMagick with only an extension check and no explicit input coder (`#{path}[0]` rather than e.g. `png:path`), so ImageMagick sniffs the real format; a '.png' that is really SVG/MVG/MSL can reach the dangerous coders (file read, SSRF), and decompression bombs are not limited (no -limit or policy). Pin the input coder to an allowlist and set resource limits.
MiniMagick.convert runs synchronously in the request thread with no MiniMagick timeout set, so a pathological image can block a Puma thread indefinitely.

DELETE /files/:name (like the other endpoints) has no authentication, so anyone who can reach the service can delete any stored file. The README admits there is no auth, but a destructive endpoint with no access control would block a production PR.

The only test that generates a thumbnail is skipped when ImageMagick isn't detected, and the detection helper rescues every error as 'not installed'. On CI the core thumbnail feature can therefore go untested without anyone noticing; it should fail or be a required CI job.
